prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1176; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is regarding the collision you were involved in on a roadway in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just go by my first name for now, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving and what you were doing just before the collision?

A: I was heading east on the main road toward the shopping center. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me, so I was already stopped at a light when it happened.

Q: Did you have any warning before the impact?

A: Not really. I looked in my mirror and saw the headlights getting closer, but there was no time to do anything. The other car hit me from behind.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: How fast would you estimate the other vehicle was traveling at impact?

A: I honestly couldn't tell you. It didn't seem like a huge speed, but the jolt was strong enough to push my car forward into the intersection.

Q: Did you experience any injuries at the scene?

A: I was sore right away, mostly in my lower back. I didn't think much of it at first, but it got worse over the next day.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care and was told I had a back strain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week and taking it easy at work.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Just that I'm still having stiffness when I get up in the morning, and I want to make sure my treatment costs get covered.

Q: Thank you. This concludes our recorded statement.

A: Thank you.
